_comment: MLA prefill shapes for gfx942. Two regimes, tagged per shape by the 'regime' key -- see _regime_note. Covers DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.1/R1 (Hq=128) and Kimi-K2 (Hq=64). Canonical MLA geometry: qk_nope=128, qk_rope=64, v_head_dim=128, kv_lora_rank=512, q_lora_rank=1536, Hkv=1. block_size=16. bf16 only on gfx942 (fp8 is gfx950+ only; see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan).
_dtype_note: bf16 only. fp8 is gfx950+ Phase 2 (see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan) and is excluded from gfx942 entirely.
_regime_note: Every shape carries a 'regime' key: 'full_prompt' (seqlen_q == seqlen_k) or 'chunked' (seqlen_q << seqlen_k). DESIGN.md S2.5 defines two prefill strategies split at seqlen_q ~200 -- in-loop latent expansion (S3 kernel) below, materialize K/V then standard flash (S3.1) above -- and S9 rows 1-4 scope both plus the dispatch between them. The full_prompt family alone measures only the materialize side: every one of its shapes has seqlen_q = seqlen_k >= 512, so the S3 kernel is never measured in the regime it exists for. An earlier revision of this file shipped only that family. The chunked family is what brackets the threshold (seqlen_q 128 below it, 256 just above, 512 well above), what makes seqlen_q != seqlen_k at all (the cu_seqlens_k path of S3, unexercised by a square mask), and what tests S2.5's 1/seqlen_q prediction that materialize degrades as the chunk shrinks against a fixed context. Report the two families separately; a full_prompt number is not evidence about the chunked regime. If the two strategies land within noise across the whole chunked family, S2.5's two-branch dispatch is unjustified -- record that and amend the design rather than shipping a dispatch between equivalents.
_batch_note: The batch axis here is deliberately narrower than the decode files' B in {1,4,8,32}, and it is measuring a different thing. Decode needs batch because the pre-step is batch-invariant while the flash loop is not, so the two crossovers of DESIGN.md S4 only appear across B. Prefill has no such BATCH crossover -- its seqlen_q crossover is S2.5's, swept on the seqlen_q axis of the chunked family above, not on this one: its pre-kernel amortizes over total_q = batch * seqlen_q, so batch and seqlen_q are interchangeable for it and a uniform-length batch sweep re-measures points the seqlen sweep already covers, at multiplied cost. What batch does buy at prefill is coverage of the packed-varlen path -- cu_seqlens_q/cu_seqlens_k prefix sums and the per-sequence causal mask -- which B=1 exercises only trivially. Hence B=4 at the two short full_prompt lengths and at one chunked point, where that coverage is cheapest, and B=1 elsewhere. Mixed sequence lengths within a batch are the case that most needs covering and this schema cannot express them; that belongs with the runner work (DESIGN.md S9).
_harness_note: These shapes are a specification for a future MLA runner, not runnable input for the current one. The existing prefill harness loads ndjson UAShape records via _ua_shape_utils.load_shapes, not this nested-object JSON, so it parses zero shapes from this file and does so silently (undecodable lines are skipped). It also requires a per-shape 'head_size', which MLA has no single value for: d_nope+d_rope=192 for the score, d_V=128 for the output. Wiring MLA shapes into a runner is part of the kernel deliverable (DESIGN.md S9).

models._note: Hq=64 (differs from DeepSeek Hq=128); all other MLA geometry is identical.
